articles.title: Remembrance Sunday services planned across Rochdale borough
articles.excerpt: Residents will gather on November 8 to honour those who served in the armed forces, with parades and services in multiple towns.
articles.content_html:
Residents across the Rochdale borough are set to come together on Sunday, November 8, to pay their respects to those who have made sacrifices defending the country. Remembrance Day commemorations will feature a series of services and parades in towns including Rochdale, Castleton, Heywood, Littleborough, Middleton, Milnrow, Norden, and Wardle.

The events will see representatives from the Navy, Army, and Royal Air Force join veterans and civic dignitaries. Each service will include hymns, prayers, the Last Post, a two-minute silence, and the national anthem, ensuring a solemn tribute to those who served.

In Heywood, the parade will commence at 10.15am on Tower Street, proceeding to St James’ Street before arriving at Heywood Memorial Gardens for a service at 10.55am. Similarly, in Middleton, the parade will gather at 10.10am facing the Harbord Harbord pub, departing for Middleton Remembrance Gardens at 10.20am, with the service starting at 10.45am.

In Rochdale, participants will assemble outside The Flying Horse Hotel in Packer Street at 10.30am, where they will be joined by ward councillors and other civic guests. The parade will march to the Cenotaph for the service at 10.55am, followed by a march past before returning to The Flying Horse Hotel.

articles.title: Rochdale mum diagnosed with breast cancer after routine NHS screening
articles.excerpt: Sarah Hickman, 50, encourages women to attend NHS breast screenings after her cancer was detected early during a routine mammogram.
articles.content_html:
A Rochdale mother, Sarah Hickman, has been diagnosed with breast cancer following a routine NHS screening, prompting her to urge other women to attend their appointments. At 50 years old, Sarah received her invitation for a mammogram and attended without any health concerns. However, just a day later, she was called back for further tests at the Breast Unit at Bolton NHS Foundation Trust.

After undergoing additional imaging, an ultrasound, and a biopsy, doctors confirmed that Sarah had a small breast cancer detected at a very early stage. Reflecting on her experience, she described it as a 'textbook case' and expressed gratitude for the NHS screening process, which allowed for early detection before any symptoms appeared.

Sarah's case highlights the importance of regular breast screenings, especially for women aged 50 and over, who are invited for routine mammograms every three years. Early detection can significantly improve treatment outcomes and survival rates, making it crucial for women to take these invitations seriously.

As Sarah continues her treatment, she hopes her story will encourage others to prioritise their health and attend NHS screenings. Women in Rochdale and beyond are reminded that these screenings can save lives, and they should not hesitate to book their appointments.

articles.excerpt: GMFRS says firefighters attended for around two hours and 40 minutes after concerns about a building structure. The road's reopening remains unconfirmed.

Update: 12.55pm GMT, Sunday 25 October 2026

The fire service said one engine from Heywood was called at about 6.30pm on Saturday. Crews inspected the building and made the area safe alongside Greater Manchester Police and Rochdale Council.

The Bury Times also reported that police attended to help manage the cordon. Emergency services have not confirmed that the storm caused the structural concerns.

The reports reviewed do not confirm when Bridge Street reopened or provide information about injuries. The precise building has not been identified. The end of firefighters' attendance does not establish that the road reopened.

Earlier update: 11.31pm BST, Saturday 24 October 2026

The Manchester Evening News reported concerns that strong winds could cause a derelict building to collapse. Its 9.20pm BST update said the area had been made safe, the building was still standing and firefighters remained at the scene when that report was issued.

Earlier report: 9.25pm BST, Saturday 24 October 2026

the source reported that Bridge Street was closed by emergency services. Its photographs showed a police cordon, a marked police car blocking access and a fire engine.

Anyone encountering restrictions should follow directions from emergency services. Further confirmed information about the road will be added to this article.

The number of HMOs has been increasing in Rochdale, raising concerns about tenant safety and compliance with housing regulations. By reporting issues, residents can assist the council in taking appropriate action against non-compliant landlords.

For more information or to report a concern, residents can visit the Rochdale Borough Council's website or email housing.standards@rochdale.gov.uk.
